summary: A notice cancelling the Resource Notebook Framework meeting that had tentatively been set for March 19, 1973, with more information on the framework from RFC 464 promised soon. It lists the NIC contacts for questions.

plainLanguage.summary: A short note saying a planned meeting will not happen, with names to ask if you have questions.

subtitle: Cancellation notice for the Resource Notebook Framework meeting scheduled for March 19, 1973.

tldr.problem: A meeting on the Resource Notebook Framework had been tentatively scheduled for March 19, 1973.
tldr.mechanism: The NIC announced the cancellation of that meeting via this brief RFC.
tldr.outcome: Future information about the Resource Notebook Framework would be distributed separately. Interested parties were directed to contact the NIC.

today: RFC 483 is a historical administrative notice. The Resource Notebook Framework is not documented in surviving records.

sections.title: Meeting Cancellation
sections.content: This RFC announces the cancellation of the Resource Notebook Framework meeting that had been tentatively scheduled for March 19, 1973. For background, interested parties are referred to RFC 464.
sections.plainLanguage: A meeting that was planned is not happening anymore.

sections.title: Future Information
sections.content: Further information concerning the Resource Notebook Framework, which was discussed in RFC 464, would be distributed soon. Those with questions could contact Jake Feinler or Mike Kudlick at the NIC by telephone at (415) 326-6200.
sections.plainLanguage: More information would come later, and the same people who canceled the meeting could answer questions.

sections.title: Resource Notebook Framework
sections.content: The Resource Notebook Framework was a proposal for organizing and sharing information resources on the ARPANET. The details had been discussed in RFC 464, and further details were to follow in later communications.
sections.plainLanguage: The Resource Notebook was an idea for how to organize and share information between different computers on the network.

references.text: Bressler, B., "Resource Notebook Framework Proposal", RFC 464, March 1973.
